thought.text: The fresh run's connection errors are teardown-time (after the health-ready probe at 21:18:06 already returned `ready`). Let me do one independent startup of the built artifact to confirm it can boot and serve.

reasoning_content:
The app logs show connection errors to Postgres/Redis at 21:18:07 — these are teardown logs after the test finished (the health-ready probe at 21:18:06 was already "ready" with db/redis/keycloak true). The connection terminated errors are at 21:18:07, after successful probes, as containers were torn down. So the app started and served health endpoints successfully before teardown.

Now let me do my own independent startup test to be thorough — boot the built artifact directly. But it requires Postgres/Redis/Keycloak env. That would need infra which doesn't exist. The verify script does it all. I already re-ran the canonical gate which does boot the real artifact with real Postgres/Redis/mock Keycloak and probes endpoints. That's strong evidence.

Let me attempt a minimal independent startup to at least confirm the artifact starts (even without DB, the health/live endpoint should respond). Actually, the entry may fail without env. But I could test that the server process at least starts listening. Let me try running it briefly with minimal env on a free port and curl /health/live. This is permitted (startup, no install/build).

Let me try.

action.command:
cd /workspace/apps/sva-studio-react && node -e "const m=require('node:fs').readFileSync('.output/server/index.mjs','utf8'); console.log('entry bytes',m.length); console.log('imports server chunk:', m.includes('_ssr/server'));" ; echo "--- start attempt on port 3111 ---"; timeout 25 env PORT=3111 SVA_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:3111 IAM_DATABASE_URL=postgres://x:x@127.0.0.1:1/x REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:1 node .output/server/index.mjs >/tmp/boot.log 2>&1 & 
BGPID=$!; sleep 12; echo "--- curl health/live ---"; curl -s -m 4 -o /tmp/live.txt -w "HTTP=%{http_code}\n" http://127.0.0.1:3111/health/live; cat /tmp/live.txt 2>/dev/null; echo; echo "--- boot log head ---"; head -20 /tmp/boot.log; kill $BGPID 2>/dev/null; wait 2>/dev/null; echo done
